lines.label: B1
lines.reason: Plate 2 to long side flange 4: a real 90 deg fold (89.6 deg), flange about 8 mm deep. In my perpendicular sections at 25/50/75% the label sits on the outer-skin apex, within +0.005/-0.008/+0.006 mm along the bisector; the nearest scan points are 0.09-0.27 mm away. A 1 mm station sweep shows the fold present from t=0 to about 38.3 mm. Past t=39 there is only the flat plate corner beyond the flange-end relief, so the extent of 38.1 mm covers the whole fold. The line is parallel to the fold.

missing_bends: M1: the bend between plate 2 and the end leg 5/6 (the lower-right leg past the U cut-out) is missing, at about 10.7 deg. The leg turns down, the same way as the flanges. The labeler left it out because of the old 15 deg rule, but under the owner's 10 deg rule (2026-10-18) it counts. Patch normals give 10.73 deg; my slope sweep at six stations across the leg width (u=2/5/8/11/14/17 mm) measured the leg at 10.4-11.0 deg against a flat plate (0 +/- 0.4 deg). The angle stays the same across the full width. Both sides are flat planes (patch 6 rms 0.005 mm), and the transition is a single straight line at constant position. The curved zone is about 3-4 mm wide, which is normal for a shallow air bend. This is a formed bend, not a rolled kink or warp. It also explains the human-backed legacy count of 4, which the labeler noted. Outer apex (top skin) in source_ply_raw coordinates: about [-173.39,-98.98,157.21] to [-155.51,-94.68,156.65]. It is parallel to B1 and sits about 15.65 mm in from the plate centroid. The fold spans the full leg width, about u = -1.2 to 19.4 in my plate frame (roughly 20.5 mm), so the line should run from the leg's left edge to its right edge. The 0.8-19.2 segment above covers only about 90%.
